lessons.title: Lesson 1: A clear service menu
lessons.text:
Lesson 1 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Write a service menu with clear descriptions and prices.
This lesson builds toward: Given your real services and prices, you will write a service menu that lists what is included, what costs extra and the price, with every price and inclusion checked by you.
Customers want to know what you do and roughly what it costs before they call. A service menu lists each service, what is included, how long it takes and the price or price range.
Give AI your real services and prices: "Write a service menu for my house-cleaning business: standard clean $120 for up to 2 bedrooms, deep clean $220, move-out clean from $260. Include what is included in each. Simple words." Check everything, especially what is and is not included.
Clear menus cut down on arguments later. Say plainly what costs extra (inside the oven, pet hair, stairs, travel over 15 miles).
Step by step:
- List your services and real prices.
- Write what is included and what costs extra.
- Ask AI to format a clear menu.
- Check every price and inclusion.
Words to know:
- Service menu: a list of the services you offer with what is included and the price.
- Add-on: an extra service that costs more.
Try it now: Write your service menu with at least three services, what is included and add-ons. Use AI to format it, then check every price.
You can now write a clear service menu with inclusions, add-ons and prices.

check.q: What does a service menu list for each service?
options: What is included, how long it takes and the price
Only the name of the service
Your home address and ID number
check.why: A service menu lists each service, what is included, how long it takes and the price or price range.

check.q: AI's menu says a deep clean includes inside the oven, but you charge extra for that. What do you do?
options: Change it to say inside the oven costs extra
check.why: You check every inclusion, and saying plainly what costs extra prevents arguments later.

lessons.title: Lesson 2: Writing quotes and estimates
lessons.text:
Lesson 2 of 6 · about 6 minutes
Goal: Make a quote template that is clear, fair and protects you.
This lesson builds toward: Given a real or sample job, you will create a quote template and fill it in with scope, price, what is not included and how long it is good for, with the price set from your own costs plus profit.
A quote says exactly what you will do, for how much, and under what conditions. A good one has: customer and job address, scope of work (what you will do), materials, price, what is not included, payment terms, when work will start and how long the quote is good for.
Ask AI to make a template: "Make a one-page quote template for a small painting business with blanks for [customer], [address], [scope], [materials], [price], [not included], [payment terms], [valid until]." Save it in Docs or Word.
AI can help you describe the scope clearly, but you set the price from your own costs: materials, your hours, travel and profit. For larger jobs, contracts and licensing rules depend on your state and trade, so check your state's contractor licensing board or a professional.
Step by step:
- Ask AI for a quote template with blanks.
- Fill in a real or sample job.
- Set the price from your costs plus profit.
- List what is not included and how long the quote is good for.
- Check licensing and contract rules for bigger jobs.
Words to know:
- Quote: a written price for a specific job.
- Scope of work: exactly what you will and will not do on a job.
- Payment terms: when and how the customer pays, such as a deposit and the rest on completion.
Try it now: Make your quote template with AI, then fill it in for one real or sample job. Work out the price on paper from your costs.
You can now write a clear quote that sets the scope, price and terms.

check.q: What does "payment terms" on a quote tell the customer?
options: What paint color you will use
How long the job will last
check.why: Payment terms say how and when the customer pays.

check.q: AI suggests a price for your painting quote. What do you do?
options: Use it because AI knows the market
Set the price yourself from materials, hours, travel and profit
check.why: AI can help describe the scope, but you set the price from your own costs.

lessons.title: Lesson 3: Answering new leads fast
lessons.text:
Lesson 3 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Reply to new inquiries quickly with templates that ask the right questions.
This lesson builds toward: Given a new inquiry by text, email, social message or missed call, you will write a first-reply template that thanks the person, asks the questions you need and gives a next step, with no request for card numbers or ID.
The first business to reply often wins the job. Have a template ready for each way people reach you: text, email, social messages and missed calls.
A good first reply thanks them, asks the two or three questions you need to quote ("How many bedrooms? Any pets? Which day works?"), and gives a next step. Ask AI to write one for each channel in your voice.
Keep templates on your phone so you can reply between jobs. Do not ask people to send card numbers or ID by text or social messages.
Step by step:
- List the questions you need to quote.
- Ask AI for a first-reply template for each channel.
- Save them on your phone.
- Reply within an hour when you can.
Words to know:
- Lead: a person who asked about your service but has not booked yet.
- Channel: a way customers reach you, like text, email or social messages.
Try it now: Write your three must-ask questions. Ask AI for a first-reply text and email template in your voice, and save them on your phone.
You can now answer new leads fast with templates that gather what you need to quote.

check.q: Where should you keep your first-reply templates?
options: On your phone so you can reply between jobs
check.why: Keeping templates on your phone lets you reply fast between jobs.

check.q: A new lead texts, "How much for a lawn cut?" What is a good first reply?
options: "Send me your card number to book."
Thank them, ask the size of the lawn and which day works, and offer a next step
Wait until the weekend to reply
Send your full price list with no greeting
check.why: A good first reply thanks them, asks the questions you need and gives a next step.

lessons.title: Lesson 4: Booking confirmations and reminders
lessons.text:
Lesson 4 of 6 · about 4 minutes
Goal: Set up booking and reminder messages that cut no-shows.
This lesson builds toward: Given your cancellation policy, you will write a booking confirmation and a day-before reminder, with the date, time window, address, price and policy included.
No-shows and lockouts cost you a day's pay. Clear confirmations and reminders help. A confirmation says the date, time window, address, price, what the customer should do to prepare and your cancellation policy.
Ask AI: "Write a booking confirmation and a reminder for the day before for my mobile dog grooming business. Blanks: [name], [date], [time window], [address], [price]. Include our 24-hour cancellation policy."
Many booking tools can send reminders automatically; check your tool's settings. If you send marketing texts or emails (not just reminders), get permission first and follow the email rules, including an unsubscribe option.
Step by step:
- Write your cancellation policy.
- Ask AI for a confirmation and a reminder template.
- Set automatic reminders in your booking tool if it has them.
- Send marketing only with permission and an unsubscribe.
Words to know:
- No-show: a customer who misses a booked appointment.
- Cancellation policy: your rules for cancelling, such as 24 hours' notice.
- Time window: a range of arrival times, like 9 to 11 am.
Official sources:
- FTC: CAN-SPAM Act, A Compliance Guide for Business
Try it now: Write your cancellation policy in two lines. Ask AI for a confirmation and a day-before reminder template with blanks, and save them.
You can now send booking confirmations and reminders that reduce no-shows.

check.q: What problem do confirmations and reminders help prevent?
check.why: The lesson says no-shows and lockouts cost a day's pay, and reminders help cut them.

check.q: You want to text all past customers a holiday discount. What do you need first?
options: Nothing; reminders and marketing are the same
Their permission, and an unsubscribe option
check.why: Marketing messages, unlike reminders, need permission and an unsubscribe option.

lessons.title: Lesson 5: Job checklists for the same quality every time
lessons.text:
Lesson 5 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Turn your know-how into a job checklist you and your helpers follow.
This lesson builds toward: Given your most common job, you will create a job checklist for before you arrive, on site and before you leave, with your trade's safety steps and a final walk-through included.
A checklist makes every job as good as your best one, even on a tired day or when a helper does it. It also helps you train new people.
Talk or type out how you do your most common job, start to finish, and ask AI: "Turn these notes into a job checklist for a standard residential lawn service: before you arrive, on site, before you leave. Short steps." Add safety steps your trade requires, and check them against official safety guidance or your trade training.
Add a final walk-through with the customer and before-and-after photos (with their permission) to show the work.
Step by step:
- Describe your common job start to finish.
- Ask AI to turn it into a three-part checklist.
- Add your trade's safety steps.
- Add a walk-through and photos with permission.
- Test it on the next job and fix it.
Words to know:
- Checklist: a list of steps to tick off so nothing is missed.
- Walk-through: going over the finished job with the customer.
Try it now: Describe your most common job in a few lines. Ask AI to turn it into a three-part checklist, add safety steps, and use it on your next job.
You can now make and use a job checklist that keeps quality the same every time.

check.q: What are the three parts of the job checklist in this lesson?
options: Before you arrive, on site, before you leave
check.why: AI turns your notes into a three-part checklist: before you arrive, on site and before you leave.

check.q: You want to add a safety step for using a ladder. Where do you check it?
options: Ask AI and trust the answer
Official safety guidance or your trade training
Skip safety steps to save time
check.why: Safety steps are checked against official guidance or your trade training.

lessons.title: Lesson 6: Follow-up, honest reviews and repeat work
lessons.text:
Lesson 6 of 6 · about 5 minutes
Goal: Follow up after a job to earn honest reviews, referrals and repeat bookings.
This lesson builds toward: After finishing a job, you will write a follow-up message that thanks the customer and asks for an honest review, a referral and the next booking, following the FTC review rule.
The job is not over when you leave. A thank-you message the same day, with a link to leave a review and an offer to book the next visit, brings repeat work. Ask AI to write it in your voice with [name] and [service] blanks.
Ask every customer the same way, happy or not, for an honest review. Do not offer rewards only for positive reviews, and never write fake ones; the FTC's review rule bans both.
Set reminders for repeat services: gutters every fall, a haircut every three weeks, a furnace check every year. A short "Time for your next...?" message keeps your calendar full.
Step by step:
- Send a thank-you the same day.
- Include a review link and ask for honest reviews.
- Offer the next booking.
- Set reminders for repeat services.
Words to know:
- Referral: a customer sending a friend to you.
- Repeat service: a job customers need again on a schedule.
Official sources:
- FTC: Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule, Questions and Answers
Try it now: Final task: put your service kit together: service menu, quote template, first-reply, confirmation and reminder templates, a job checklist, and a follow-up thank-you with a review request and next-booking offer.
You can now run a service business's paperwork from first call to repeat customer with AI help.
How your final task is checked:
What we look at Not yet Meets Exceeds Clear service menu Prices or inclusions are missing or wrong. Each service lists what is included, what costs extra and the price. Also shows how long each service takes and any add-ons. Complete quote template The quote is missing scope, price, what is not included or how long it is good for. All parts are there and the price comes from your costs plus profit. Also has payment terms and a note on where licensing rules were checked for bigger jobs. Booking messages The confirmation or reminder is missing the time window, address or cancellation policy. Confirmation and day-before reminder with date, time window, address, price and policy. Also tells the customer how to prepare and is set to send automatically. Job checklist The checklist skips steps or has no safety steps. Three-part checklist with safety steps and a final walk-through. Tested on a real job and fixed afterward. Honest follow-up The message offers a reward only for good reviews or has no review request. Thanks the customer, asks for an honest review and referral, and offers the next booking. Also sets a reminder for the next repeat service. To pass: Meets or Exceeds on every row. If a row is Not yet, fix that part and try again.

check.q: When should you send a thank-you message after a job?
check.why: A thank-you the same day, with a review link and next-booking offer, brings repeat work.

check.q: A customer was unhappy with part of the job. How do you ask for a review?
options: Do not ask them at all
Offer a discount only if they give 5 stars
Write a good review for them
Ask them the same way as everyone for an honest review
check.why: You ask every customer the same way for an honest review; rewards only for positive reviews are banned.
